payout_quote: Our web-based marketplace lets graphic designers (including studios, professional designers, work-from-home designers, student graphic designers and freelance designers) respond to these briefs, win work and earn money.
steps: Create a free DesignCrowd designer account with a portfolio and payment preferences.
Browse available design projects (contests and one-on-one jobs) matching your skills.
Read the client brief carefully and submit original design concepts.
If the client selects your design, payment lands in your DesignCrowd account; withdraw via PayPal, Payoneer, or bank transfer.
Build ratings and repeat-client relationships to win more often.
catches: Contest work is speculative: only the selected designer is paid per contest; most submissions earn nothing.
Project budgets (and therefore payouts) are set per brief by the client — no fixed amounts.
DesignCrowd takes a 15% commission from the total project amount (per third-party fee reporting; confirm in current terms).
Fierce competition from a large global designer pool; winning consistently is hard.
Original work only — using others' images or AI-generated images can get your account deactivated.
biggest_catch: Most contest entries earn nothing: only the client-selected design is paid, so expected payout per entry is low and losing work is unpaid.
eligibility: Free designer account; must submit original work and hold copyright to submitted images.
timing: Projects run on client-set deadlines; payout after selection, withdrawable via PayPal/Payoneer/bank transfer.

c1.evidence: DesignCrowd's own help center (designcrowd.com/help) states the mechanism: designers 'respond to these briefs, win work and earn money' via Design Contests or One-on-one Jobs.

c2.evidence: Official terms tie payout to winning/selection per project; no fixed payout range published — framed as variable.

c3.evidence: Steps follow the official flow: profile, browse projects, submit concepts, get selected, receive payment.

c4.evidence: Creating an account and entering contests is free; the platform's commission comes out of project amounts, not upfront.

s1.note: Eligibility is a free designer account; effectively gated by design skill.

s2.note: Framed as variable per-project pay; no fixed amount promised.

s3.note: Catches cover unpaid losing entries, client-set budgets, and the 15% commission.

s4.note: Deduped: no DesignCrowd route in qa/existing-providers.txt, dedupe-check.py, or qa/verification/*.json.
